record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.context_brief: QGP formation in AGS baryon-rich fireballs
record.original_question: In dense baryon-rich matter fireballs produced at BNL AGS energies, is a quark-gluon plasma formed, and can measurements of strange antibaryon production distinguish QGP formation from final-state confined-matter chemical equilibration?

evidence.quote: In principle, this is not in contradiction to possible formation of deconfined baryon rich quark matter at AGS energies, since hadronic abundance equilibration could be just a final state effect. Moreover, since for AGS energies it is expected that the specific entropy per baryon in confined and deconfined matter is very similar, there is to this date no clear evidence for, or against, QGP formation in the dense baryon rich matter fireballs made at AGS. The forthcoming measurement of strange antibaryon production should resolve this issue in the near future.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider heavy-ion collisions at fixed-target energies on the order of about 10 GeV per nucleon (energies characteristic of dense, baryon-rich fireballs), in which strongly interacting matter is compressed to high baryon density. In such collisions, two competing scenarios for strange-hadron production are considered:

(a) A deconfined quark-gluon plasma (QGP) phase is transiently formed, and strange and antistrange quarks produced in the deconfined phase hadronize into the observed final-state strange (anti)baryons; or

(b) No deconfined phase is formed, and the observed strange-hadron abundances arise from chemical equilibration in a purely hadronic (confined) final state.

Assume that the specific entropy per baryon in the confined and deconfined scenarios is approximately equal at these energies, so that bulk thermodynamic observables alone cannot easily discriminate between (a) and (b).

The problem is twofold:

1. Determine whether a quark-gluon plasma is in fact formed in dense, baryon-rich fireballs produced in heavy-ion collisions at these energies.

2. Determine whether measurements of strange antibaryon production (for example, yields, ratios, and excitation functions of antihyperons such as $\bar{\Lambda}$, $\bar{\Xi}$, and $\bar{\Omega}$) provide observables that can rigorously discriminate scenario (a) from scenario (b), and exhibit explicit signatures (e.g. characteristic hierarchies of yield ratios or features of the energy-dependence) whose presence or absence in experimental data settles the question in (1).
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent literature notes that the experimental detector capability needed to measure strange antibaryons at the AGS only became available near the end of the AGS heavy-ion program, and the available results did not permit a convincing evaluation of QGP formation in baryon-rich fireballs at AGS energies. While strangeness and strange-antibaryon enhancement have since contributed to the QGP discovery narrative at higher (SPS/RHIC) energies, the specific AGS-energy question of QGP formation in dense baryon-rich matter remains without a definitive experimental resolution.

status_evidence.title: Discovery of Quark-Gluon-Plasma: Strangeness Diaries
status_evidence.snippet: it is hard to tell what exactly was the AGS discovery potential of QGP, since only after 15 years the needed detector equipment became available to look for strange antibaryons, and when this was just before the AGS experimental program was shut, the results made available were not allowing a convincing evaluation
status_evidence.claim: The AGS strange-antibaryon measurements did not yield a conclusive determination of QGP formation in baryon-rich fireballs.

status_evidence.title: Energy Dependence of Strange Particle Yields from a QGP-Fireball
status_evidence.snippet: Strange antibaryon excitation functions are shown to have characteristic features that should allow to discriminate between the QGP hypothesis and other reaction scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical proposals identify strange antibaryon excitation functions as discriminators between QGP and hadronic scenarios.
